title: 2026-10-22_Xbash_Incident_Response_63b
description: Investigate and respond to a potential Xbash malware infection combining ransomware, coinmining, and botnet capabilities.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity on its Linux-based systems. Initial analysis suggests a potential Xbash malware infection, which combines ransomware, coinmining, and botnet capabilities. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using the provided credentials. Username: admin, Password: admin123. Start by connecting via SSH.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using the provided credentials. Username: admin, Password: admin123. Start by connecting via SSH.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Investigate the target host for any unauthorized or suspicious services running. Identify any services that appear out of place or exhibit unusual behavior.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and running processes using commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` and `ps aux`. Look for any services or processes that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and running processes.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` and `ps aux` to identify suspicious services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service identified in the previous task is automatically started after reboot. Investigate the persistence mechanisms used.
levels.solution: Look for systemd service files and timers using commands like `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled` and `ls /etc/systemd/system/*.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd service files and timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled` and `ls /etc/systemd/system/*.timer` to identify persistence mechanisms.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Identify any file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts. Investigate the lateral movement techniques employed by the attacker.
levels.solution: Check the rsync logs and SSH connections using commands like `grep rsync /var/log/syslog` and `last`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the rsync logs and SSH connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `grep rsync /var/log/syslog` and `last` to identify lateral movement techniques.
